data.note: Each rule as published, with what the recorded forecasts say at the launch time. Shares count one forecast system's runs; they are never combined. None has passed a check against observations yet.

rules.text: Do not launch for 30 minutes after lightning is observed within 10 nautical miles of the launch pad or the flight path, unless specified conditions can be met.

observed.detail: Lightning seen from space (GOES lightning mapper) is recorded only in the six hours before a launch opportunity; the range watches it at the time.

climatology.source: NASA's GLM thunder hours (GHRC DAAC): thunder could be heard in the pad's 5 km grid cell in 1 of the 217 hours of October at 08 UTC seen by the lightning mappers in those years. Thunder heard at the pad means lightning close by, not a count of the rule's own distance.

rules.text: Do not launch within 10 nautical miles of an attached thunderstorm anvil cloud, unless temperature and time-associated distance criteria can be met.

observed.detail: Decided by the range's weather officers at the time.

rules.text: Do not launch within 10 nautical miles of a detached thunderstorm anvil cloud.

observed.detail: Decided by the range's weather officers at the time.

rules.text: Do not launch within 3 nautical miles of a thunderstorm debris cloud, unless specific time-associated distance criteria can be met.

observed.detail: Decided by the range's weather officers at the time.

rules.text: Do not launch within 5 nautical miles of disturbed weather clouds that extend into freezing temperatures and contain moderate or greater precipitation, unless specific time-associated distance criteria can be met.

observed.detail: Decided by the range's weather officers at the time.

rules.text: Do not launch for 15 minutes if field mill instrument readings within five nautical miles of the launch pad exceed +/- 1,500 volts per meter, or +/- 1,000 volts per meter if specified criteria can be met.

observed.detail: The range's field mill readings are not public.

rules.text: Do not launch through a cloud layer greater than 4,500 feet thick that extends into freezing temperatures, unless other specific criteria can be met.

per_system.missing_reason: The recorded model fields (winds at 10 and 80 m, gusts, cloud cover, CAPE) do not describe this rule.
ECMWF's ensemble is not recorded yet.
ECMWF's AI ensemble (AIFS) is not recorded yet.

rules.text: Do not launch within 10 nautical miles of cumulus clouds with tops that extend into freezing temperatures, unless specific height-associated distance criteria can be met.

per_system.missing_reason: The recorded model fields (winds at 10 and 80 m, gusts, cloud cover, CAPE) do not describe this rule.
ECMWF's ensemble is not recorded yet.
ECMWF's AI ensemble (AIFS) is not recorded yet.

rules.text: Do not launch within 10 nautical miles of the edge of a thunderstorm that is producing lightning within 30 minutes after the last lightning is observed.

observed.detail: Thunderstorms are watched by the range at the time.

climatology.source: NASA's GLM thunder hours (GHRC DAAC): thunder could be heard in the pad's 5 km grid cell in 1 of the 217 hours of October at 08 UTC seen by the lightning mappers in those years. Thunder heard at the pad means lightning close by, not a count of the rule's own distance.

rules.text: Do not launch through cumulus clouds formed as the result of or directly attached to a smoke plume, unless time-associated criteria can be met.

limit.missing_reason: The limit is not published; the team can enter the one it is given. No unit is published for it, so any unit is taken.

observed.detail: Decided by the range's weather officers at the time.

data.range_note: Launches from the same range within a day of this one, from Launch Library 2.

parts.note: k of N runs break the rule at the forecast step nearest the launch (within 3 hours); the ± is the exact 95 % interval for that many runs.
Winds at the rule's height are interpolated from the model's 10 m and 80 m winds on a logarithmic profile.
No rule has been checked against observations yet, so each share says so.
